clue.text: Drinks round after round

definitions.meaning: ... up, as a cat takes in milk with its tongue

explanation.definitionFit: A cat lapping is drinking with its tongue, and a runner completing circuit after circuit of a track clocks up several of them.

clue.text: Stick-like creature's swarming in fleas, etc

indicators.note: swarming insects move about in a mass, so the letters jumble together

explanation.surface: An insect resembling a twig moves about among fleas and other bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swarming' rearranges IN FLEAS ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaf insects are tropical insects camouflaged as foliage, close relatives of the twig-like stick insects.

clue.text: Took steps to assist an athlete

definitions.meaning: walked with measured strides, back and forth
to set the speed for a runner as a pacemaker does

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who walked up and down measured out strides, and a pacemaker in a race helps a runner by setting the speed.

clue.text: Bones deployed in bands?

parts.note: the bones are the leg joints of a chicken, but the same word names the sticks a percussionist wields in a marching band

explanation.definitionFit: The lower leg of a cooked bird shares its name with the beaters used on a drum kit, which bands certainly deploy.

clue.text: Fruit that's dried, although is in the monsoon

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the monsoon is the season of heavy rains
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fruit gets dried, even though it sits in the wet season.
explanation.walkthrough: The contrast of dried fruit with the wet season is the misdirection; 'in' signals the insertion and 'although' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Raisins are grapes that have been dried.

clue.text: Frenzied women made amends, awkwardly embracing academician

indicators.note: holding one piece in its arms, so it surrounds the other
the letters of amends are arranged clumsily into a new order

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for academician, as in RA

explanation.surface: Wild women apologised clumsily while hugging a member of the Academy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges AMENDS to MAENDS and 'embracing' puts A inside. 'made' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Maenads were the female followers of Dionysus who worked themselves into ecstatic frenzy.

clue.text: I don't fancy carving in circles

definitions.note: singular in the clue, standing for the class of round artworks

indicators.note: to fancy is to imagine, so the letters are reimagined in another order

explanation.surface: Someone says they don't care for carving in a round shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges I DON'T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tondo is a circular painting or relief sculpture, and the Italian plural names such round works.

clue.text: Many aunt rose schooled, as a mistress

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

indicators.note: trained, shaped into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aunt called Rose taught many to behave like a kept woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'schooled' rearranges AUNT ROSE to OURTESAN, after C. 'as a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan was a woman kept by a wealthy lover, a mistress of high society.

clue.text: Sliding light fixture

parts.note: sounds like a lamp fitting that moves, but describes the frame holding a window's glass that slides up and down

explanation.definitionFit: In a sash window the glazed frame slides vertically, and a light is an old word for a windowpane.

clue.text: Neighbourhood gang's with drunken moll round cab

indicators.note: drunken movement is unsteady, so these letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: The local gang are out with a tipsy girlfriend circling a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' rearranges MOLL, O and CAB together. ''s with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang of toughs from the immediate area is a band of local troublemakers.

clue.text: A solitary person will have a job to conceal it

parts.note: the indefinite article, written an in its other form

indicators.note: concealing something means wrapping it out of sight, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a chore is a routine job
taken as written

explanation.surface: A loner will struggle to keep a secret hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to conceal' puts IT inside CHORE; the second 'a' stands for AN, the same article in its form before a vowel. 'will have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorite is a religious recluse who withdraws from the world to live alone in a cell.

clue.text: Can't be proper if they are common

definitions.text: Can't be proper if they are common

parts.words: Can't be proper if they are common
parts.note: reads like a remark on manners or class, but describes the grammatical split between proper and common types of naming word

explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, naming words are either proper (capitalised names) or common (general things), so a common one is by definition not proper.

clue.text: I'm first, and I change here for the eastern region

indicators.note: says that the letter I stands at the front of the answer

parts.note: the clue's I'm, read as the letter I

indicators.note: the letters of and I change their order, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A traveller explains that they connect here for the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm first' puts I at the front; 'change' rearranges AND I to NDIA. The surface plays on changing trains.
explanation.definitionFit: The subcontinent lies to the east of Europe and is often spoken of as a region of the East.

clue.text: Stigma is spelled out in plain, clear language such poets favour

definitions.text: plain, clear language such poets favour

indicators.note: the letters of stigma is are set out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A mark of disgrace is explained in simple terms, the way certain poets like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelled out' rearranges STIGMA IS. The definition is descriptive: the poets who favoured plain, precise language were the early twentieth-century movement of Pound and others.
explanation.definitionFit: The Imagist movement of Ezra Pound and Hilda Doolittle championed exact, concrete, uncluttered language in verse.

clue.text: In particular pieces, played by associate

indicators.note: pieces played are moved about, so the letters change order

parts.note: an ally is an associate or partner

explanation.surface: Particular pieces of music are performed by a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges PIECES to ESPECI, followed by ALLY. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Especially means particularly, singling something out above others.

clue.text: Plots movement of endless chessmen

indicators.note: the letters move around into a new arrangement
the word chessmen loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A chess player plots the endless shuffling of pieces on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final N of CHESSMEN, and 'movement of' rearranges CHESSME.
explanation.definitionFit: Schemes are secret plans or plots, as in schemes against a rival.

clue.text: Result of a most successful drive

definitions.text: Result of a most successful drive

parts.words: Result of a most successful drive
parts.note: could be any campaign or journey, but the drive is a golfer's tee shot reaching the cup at once

explanation.definitionFit: A golfer who sinks the ball from the tee with a single stroke achieves the rarest of shots.

clue.text: Cavities utilised in a ship

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
something utilised is in use

explanation.surface: Hollow spaces are put to use aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinuses are air-filled hollows in the skull bones behind the face.

clue.text: Small man holding weapon grew closer

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Ned is a short form of Edward, so a small version of a man's name
an arrow is a weapon

explanation.surface: A short man clutching a weapon edged nearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small man' is a short form of a man's name, Ned for Edward; 'holding' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: When a gap narrowed, its two sides came nearer to each other.

clue.text: Monkey seen to pass round vehicle

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
O is round in shape
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A monkey is spotted getting past a car on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The colobus is an African leaf-eating primate with long silky fur.

clue.text: Deployment of hose and a mop pointless for this cleansing operation

indicators.note: deploying spreads things out in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged
a compass point, E for east, is dropped from the letters

explanation.surface: Using a hose and a mop is pointless for this kind of washing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' drops E (east, a compass point) from HOSE A MOP, and 'Deployment of' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampooing is the washing of hair or carpet with a soapy liquid, a cleaning procedure.

clue.text: Yes, somehow about to call for a fluid extractor

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other
the letters of yes are muddled into a new order

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to phone for a device that draws off liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the letters to SYE, and 'about' wraps those around the call; 'to' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A syringe draws liquid up through its nozzle by pulling back the plunger.

clue.text: Sea creatures wrecking ships carrying marine force

indicators.note: wrecked ships are broken up, so the letters are shuffled into a new order
the ships carry the marines aboard, so the marine force joins the ship letters in the pool to be rearranged

parts.note: RM stands for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Sea creatures wreck vessels transporting a body of marines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecking' rearranges SHIPS together with RM (Royal Marines), which the ships are 'carrying'; the R and M end up apart in the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimps are small swimming crustaceans found in the sea.

clue.text: Is around, unfortunately, but is well out of date

definitions.note: a phrase used for a noun: something or someone hopelessly old-fashioned

indicators.note: the letters of is around are arranged badly, into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is still about, sadly, though hopelessly behind the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges IS AROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a dinosaur is a person or thing that is outdated and has failed to adapt.

clue.text: Bulb, to be operative, needs charge

parts.note: a machine that is on is working or operative
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: A light bulb needs electrical charge to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' suggests a lamp; it is the vegetable. 'to be' and 'needs' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is the edible bulb of a plant of the lily family.

clue.text: Daggers drawn

parts.note: suggests hostility, but the daggers are printed marks drawn on a page

explanation.definitionFit: The obelus is the printer's dagger symbol used for footnotes, so the plural refers to such marks written down.

clue.text: Bondsman

parts.note: looks like a word for a serf or guarantor, but names the machine that picks winning savings certificates

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, Premium Bonds are savings certificates entered in a monthly prize draw; the winning numbers are chosen by a random-number machine with a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment selects the prize-winning Premium Bonds, making it the man of the bonds.

clue.text: Intimate the weaponry's turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the letters from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: weaponry is guns, with the 's standing for is

explanation.surface: Someone hints that the arms have arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses GUNS. 'Intimate' looks like a verb meaning to hint; it is the adjective meaning cosy.
explanation.definitionFit: A snug space is cosy and close, an intimate setting.

clue.text: I complain on rejection by her

indicators.note: being rejected means being turned back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
to moan is to complain

explanation.surface: A suitor grumbles after being turned down by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on rejection' reverses I MOAN as a whole. 'her' is the definition: a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a woman's name, so it can stand for a particular she.

clue.text: Once a much sought-after flower?

definitions.meaning: the alias of the fictional English hero hunted in revolutionary France, 'sought here, sought there'
a small red-flowered wild plant of fields

explanation.walkthrough: The Scarlet Pimpernel, hero of Baroness Orczy's novel, was sought 'here, there, everywhere'; he took his name from the small red wildflower.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet pimpernel is a small red wildflower, and the alias of Orczy's elusive hero whom the French searched for in vain.

clue.text: The last hen-grouse moved — plants provided cover here

indicators.note: the letters of hen-grouse move into a new order
take only the final letter of the word The

explanation.surface: The final hen-grouse has been relocated somewhere sheltered among the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges HENGROUSE to GREENHOUS; 'The last' adds E, the final letter of 'The'.
explanation.definitionFit: A glasshouse shelters plants from the weather, so it is the place where they are given cover.

clue.text: A cathedral right ahead? You can depend on it

indicators.note: says the first piece goes in front of the other

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: Is a cathedral straight in front? You can count on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead' puts R before ELY, a cathedral city in eastern England. 'You can ... on it' are links around the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rely on someone is to trust or depend on them.
